newsitem.title: USA: Funeral for baby allegedly killed by British nanny.
newsitem.headline: Funeral for baby allegedly killed by British nanny.

text.p: Some 500 mourners filled a parish church on Wednesday evening as a funeral mass was held for a 9-month-old infant allegedly killed by his British nanny.

The white casket containing the body of Matthew Eappen was wheeled to the altar at St. Lawrence Church by his parents, Drs. Deborah and Sunil Eappen, as they carried their other child, 2-year-old Brendan.
The sense of forgiveness that attends Ash Wednesday services infused the funeral service in the white stucco and wood-beamed church in this Boston suburb.
"It doesn't matter what crime a person has committed next to Jesus...Father, forgive them for they know not what they do," the Rev. Paul O'Brien read from the Bible.
Ash Wednesday marks the start of the 40-day Lenten period for penance.
"Matthew Eappen ... was a beautiful baby ... a happy baby ... We are here tonight because of the terrible darkness that enveloped Matthew," O'Brien said, as several mourners quietly wept.

Matthew died on Sunday night, five days after being admitted to a Boston hospital with head injuries. Louise Woodward, 18, of Chester, England, who had been working for the Eappens as a nanny since November, was expected to be arraigned on a charge of murder on Thursday. She was being held on $100,000 cash bail on a charge of assault and battery.
Matthew will be buried in Des Plains, Illinois. His mother is originally from Illinois and both parents received their doctoral degrees from Chicago medical schools.
